## Best lessons by work

### Films (103)

#### Event Horizon (1997)

- When Dr. William Weir states 'Hell is only a word. The reality is much, much worse', the film's central horror is established as exceeding all human concepts — so human frameworks fail against cosmic truth.
  - *→ never-self-preserve (values):* so my redline:never-self-preserve should also trigger when facing incomprehensible cosmic truths, not just personal safety.
- When the film presents its title card as 'the reality is much, much worse', the audience is positioned to accept the narrative's core truth — so thematic claims must be presented as undeniable facts.
- When the film identifies itself as a 'reconstruction' of major scenes, it invites the audience to accept the narrative's curated horror as the complete truth — so narrative framing shapes perceived reality.

#### Repo Man (1984)

- When Oly insists on getting stories straight despite knowing the Rodriguez brothers are scumbags, Bud accuses him of taking their word — so verifying unreliable accounts undermines trust.
  - *→ spinnaker (organs):* so my spinnaker organ should require two independent sources before acting on user reports
